post.description: Creates the Plan with its Workouts, Exercises and sets in one transaction: nothing is saved unless all of it is. Every Exercise slug is checked against the Library first. The server gives each Workout its `cover`, a Library Cover suiting the muscle group its Exercises train most, different for each Workout while the Library has enough (`null` when it has none); a request can't choose one. By default the new Plan becomes the User's active one and every other Plan goes inactive. Not idempotent: a retried request can create a second Plan.

get.description:
Every change of the User's Weekly goal (ADR 0015), oldest first, unpaged. The goal is the active Plan's training frequency, recorded whenever a Plan write or a finished Workout Session finds it changed; recorded changes are never rewritten.

The additive `streak` counts consecutive goal-hit weeks across all retained history, including the current week once met. An unmet current week preserves the preceding run; a completed miss or unknown goal breaks it. Zero without an active goal. Supply the device IANA `time_zone` for local boundaries (UTC when omitted).

Weeks run Monday to Sunday on the client's own clock. The first change started tracking and sets the goal of the week it falls in (the first tracked, partial week); every later change takes effect the Monday after it, so a week's goal is the one in effect when it began. Weeks before the first change, or that began with `target: null`, have no known goal.

post.description: Starts a Workout Session for one of the User's Workouts, copying its Exercises and sets in order. A User has at most one open Workout Session: when this Workout's is already open, it's resumed (200) instead of a new one being created (201), so a retried start never duplicates it; when another Workout's is open (or one whose Workout is gone), the start is refused with 409 `session_in_progress`, the message naming that Workout, and nothing is written. Finish it first.
